sourcedFrom: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. (UNDATED — nothing in the document states one)
cleanIntro:
The H&R T48 is a semi-automatic rifle sold under the Harrington & Richardson name, built to take metric pattern magazines. It opens like a break-open shotgun: push the takedown lever back and the upper receiver tips open on its front hinge, then the bolt carrier and bolt slide out the back.

The gas piston and its return spring sit behind a gas plug in front of the front sight base. The plug turns half a turn and comes out toward the muzzle, and the piston and spring come out after it.

The chamber is left dry, and the inside of the carrier gets no oil. The book stops at the bolt, the carrier and the gas piston.

steps.title: Safety up, on SAFE
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger outside the trigger guard. Push the safety, on the left side of the receiver above the pistol grip, up to SAFE before anything else.
steps.prose: Everything after this assumes the rifle cannot fire while you work the controls.
steps.quote: Place the safety selector on SAFE. The safety is located on the left side of the receiver above the pistol grip.
steps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.17

steps.title: Magazine out — press the latch, rock it forward
steps.action: Press in on the magazine latch, rock the bottom of the magazine toward the muzzle, and lift it out of the magazine well.
steps.prose: It rocks out; it does not drop straight down. The magazine comes out before the action is opened, or opening the action only feeds the next round.
steps.quote: Press in on the magazine latch [figure 2], rotate the base of the magazine toward the muzzle end of the rifle [Figure 3] and remove it from the magazine well.
steps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.17

steps.title: Operating rod handle back, bolt lock up
steps.action: Finger off the trigger. Pull the operating rod handle all the way back, reach across the receiver and press up on the bolt lock so the action stays open. Check the safety is still on SAFE.
steps.prose: The action has to be held open to see into the chamber.
steps.quote: With your finger off the trigger, pull the operating rod handle all the way to the rear, reach across the receiver, and press up on the bolt lock [Figure 4].
steps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.18

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber
steps.action: Look through the ejection port into the receiver and the chamber and confirm there is no cartridge in either.
steps.prose: Seeing an empty chamber is the check. Working the action is not.
steps.quote: Look into the receiver and chamber through the ejection port to verify that there are no cartridges in the chamber.
steps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.18

steps.title: Takedown lever back toward the stock
steps.action: With the rifle unloaded and on SAFE, push the takedown lever toward the buttstock.
steps.prose: The lever is what holds the two receivers closed. Nothing else needs to come off first.
steps.quote: push the takedown lever towards the buttstock of the firearm.
steps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23

steps.title: Break the receiver open
steps.action: Let the upper receiver tip open away from the lower, hinging at the front like a break-open shotgun.
steps.prose: The two halves stay joined at the front hinge. Open it far enough to reach the back of the bolt carrier.
steps.quote: This will allow the upper receiver to seperate from the lower receiver, and "shotgun" frontwards.
steps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23

steps.title: Operating rod back to show the carrier's tail
steps.action: Pull the operating rod back toward the buttstock until the tail of the bolt carrier shows at the rear of the upper.
steps.prose: The tail is what you grip in the next step.
steps.quote: pull the operating rod towards the buttstock, this will expose the “tail” of the bolt carrier.
steps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23

steps.title: Carrier and bolt out the back
steps.action: Grip the tail of the carrier and pull it straight back out of the upper. The bolt comes out with it.
steps.prose: Carrier and bolt come out together as one assembly.
steps.quote: Grasp the tail of the carrier, and pull it rearwards to remove the carrier and the bolt.
steps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23

steps.title: Dust cover off (optional)
steps.action: With the bolt carrier out, slide the dust cover back and off to open up the inside of the receiver for cleaning.
steps.prose: The book makes this optional. It only comes off once the carrier is out.
steps.quote: To remove the dust cover, simply pull rearward once the bolt carrier has been removed.
steps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the upper and lower, still joined at the front hinge; the bolt carrier with its bolt; and the dust cover if you took it off. Taking the bolt out of the carrier and pulling the gas piston are in DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Nothing else comes off for routine cleaning.
steps.quote: You can now remove the bolt from the carrier for cleaning and maintenance.
steps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23

deepSteps.title: Bolt out of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Hold the bolt carrier in one hand and turn it upside down. Push the bolt to the rear, then push it up and out of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Back first, then up. It will not lift out until it has gone to the rear.
deepSteps.quote: take bolt carrier assembly in one hand, turn upside down, push the bolt to the rear and then push the bolt up and outwards.
deepSteps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23

deepSteps.title: Gas plug: half a turn, then out toward the muzzle
deepSteps.action: Find the gas plug in front of the front sight base. Turn it 180 degrees to its removal position, then pull it forward toward the muzzle and off the rifle.
deepSteps.prose: This is the gas plug, not the adjustable gas knob — leave the gas setting where it is.
deepSteps.quote: Rotate the gas plug to the removal position (180 degrees) [Figure 19] then pull the gas plug towards the muzzle of the firearm.
deepSteps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — ADJUSTABLE GAS BLOCK INSTRUCTIONS, printed p.24

deepSteps.title: Muzzle down — piston and return spring slide out
deepSteps.action: Point the muzzle at the ground and let the gas piston and its return spring slide out.
deepSteps.prose: Work over the bench so the spring does not roll away.
deepSteps.quote: Point the muzzle towards the ground, and the piston and return spring should fall free.
deepSteps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — ADJUSTABLE GAS BLOCK INSTRUCTIONS, printed p.24

deepSteps.title: This is where the book stops
deepSteps.action: The bolt is out of the carrier and the gas piston and return spring are out. The book goes no further for routine maintenance.
deepSteps.prose: Anything past this point is for a gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: No further disassembly is required for routine maintenance.
deepSteps.cite: H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL — H&R T48 OWNERS MANUAL (title on the cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — ADJUSTABLE GAS BLOCK INSTRUCTIONS, printed p.24

cleaning.name: CHAMBER
tasks: Chamber brush with bore solvent or CLP, several passes to scrub the inside of the chamber.
Wipe with clean patches until a patch stays clean.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Patch soaked in bore cleaner through the barrel several times, starting from the chamber end.
Cleaning brush through several times with more bore cleaner to lift copper fouling and powder residue.
Patch again; if it does not come out clean, brush again until a clean patch exits.
One patch with gun oil through the bore to protect it.
Outside of the barrel with a nylon brush and cleaner-lubricant, then wipe clean.
Do not let the cleaning rod scratch the inside of the barrel or chamber.

cleaning.name: BOLT AND CARRIER
tasks: With the bolt out of the carrier, clean both with CLP or a suitable solvent.
Wipe excess oil off the bolt before reassembly.
⛔ Do not lubricate the inside of the carrier — lubricate the exterior only.

cleaning.name: GAS PISTON AND RETURN SPRING
tasks: Wipe the piston and return spring with a cloth and CLP to remove carbon fouling.
Nothing further is needed for the piston and spring.

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: With the dust cover off, the inside of the receiver is open to clean.
Wipe all metal with a clean cloth, then a lightly oiled cloth.
Use only cleaning solutions made for firearms — some solvents can damage the finish.
⚠ Excess oil or grease can raise pressure dangerously and may burst the barrel when fired — keep it light.

reassembly: Return spring and gas piston back in through the front of the gas block.
Gas plug back in and turned back from its removal position so it is held in place.
Dust cover back on, if you took it off.
Bolt carrier and bolt back into the upper from the rear.
Close the upper receiver down onto the lower until the takedown lever holds it shut.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: The book does not print a function check. With the rifle reassembled, magazine out and chamber seen empty: work the operating rod handle several times — the action should run without binding and close fully. Make sure the receiver is fully closed and held by the takedown lever, and that the gas plug is secure. If anything binds or the action will not close, do not fire it; contact the maker.
